findings.evidence: test_handle_law_in_contract and test_reuse_policy_and_arms_recorded assert only that substrings exist in the contract/table; test_plan_fields_cover_outputs and test_decorators_are_the_real_compiled_flags mix live-fact checks with text greps. None of these exercise runtime behavior.
findings.repair: Keep them, renamed *_recorded, as recording checks; require C11/C12 to enforce the corresponding laws behaviorally (trace slice validation, partial-trace status, budget recompute, handle lifetime) and never count these text checks as runtime law enforcement in any gate total.
findings.title: Law-presence assertions are not behavioral enforcement

findings.evidence: test_growth_derivation_bit_identity: the split lhs/rhs are unused; the asserted equality is 1.5/2.0 == 0.75 (trivially exact) and the fold comparison overrides growth with its own default value, so it compares identical argument vectors. test_growth_ulp_miss_is_identity_not_tolerance: the 1-ULP fold run (`near`) is computed but never asserted; the ULP claim reduces to the canonical-digest flip already covered by test_canonical.py.
findings.repair: In the derivation test, evaluate the wrapper's actual expression on two input pairs with the same real quotient but different bit results (e.g. 0.3/0.4 vs 0.75) and assert the plan records the exact quotient bits and the fold given those bits is bit-identical. In the ULP test, either assert on `near` (plan-identity digest differs; output bits may legitimately coincide) or delete the dead line and rename the test to what it actually checks.
findings.title: Dead code and vacuous assertions in two dependency tests

findings.evidence: canon.frame((1, 2)) == canon.frame([1, 2]) (isinstance(v, (list, tuple)) -> the same 'L' frame), while canonical_encoding.frame_law only names 'list'.
findings.repair: State the unification explicitly in the frame law, or admit only list and reject tuple in the encoder; pin whichever the schema means.
findings.title: Frame encoder silently unifies tuple with list

findings.evidence: frame(2**64) raises struct.error (not a contract-typed rejection); test_unframed_types_refused covers only {1: 2} and None.
findings.repair: Pin the refusal contract (accepted types, exception type for out-of-range ints) in the law text and add the out-of-range int case to the refusal test.
findings.title: Out-of-range int refusal is untyped and unpinned

findings.evidence: test_table_embeds_live_facts compares the table against _engine_facts output — the same extractor the implementation used to emit the table — so a shared extractor bug would pass. This review closed the hole independently (75/75 agreement with a different closure method).
findings.repair: Keep a permanently independent re-derivation (or golden fact digests from a second extractor) in the gate so the table is never validated only by its own emitter.
findings.title: The suite's live-facts check is self-referential to its own extractor
